questions.title: 58. What are props?
questions.summary:
◦ Props = read-only inputs passed from parent C^ → child C^.
◦ Configure C^ behavior + appearance.
questions.answer:
◦ Props = inputs received by a C^ from its parent.
◦ Configure C^ behavior, appearance, and content.
◦ Read-only snapshots for each r().
◦ Support one-way data flow: parent → child.
◦ Accept primitives, objects, arrays, F()s, and R^ elements.
◦ children represents nested content.
◦ Parent can pass cb^ props to let children request updates.
questions.underTheHood:
◦ Parent r() produces R^ elements containing props.
◦ R^ supplies props when rendering child C^.
◦ Parent re-r() normally causes child r() unless work is skipped.
◦ React.memo can skip re-r() when props remain unchanged.
◦ Default React.memo comparison checks each prop using Object.is().
◦ Primitive → value cmp.
◦ Object / Array / F() → ref cmp.
pitfalls: ◦ New {} / [] / F() refs can break memoization.
◦ key is not accessible through props.
followUps: ◦ How does child → parent communication work?
questions.recall:
◦ Props → Parent → Child.
◦ Read-only snapshot.
◦ children → nested UI.
◦ cb^ → Child requests parent update.
◦ React.memo → Object.is() per prop.

questions.title: 59. What is state?
questions.summary:
◦ State = C^ memory preserved between renders.
◦ Updates schedule re-r() and produce new UI snapshots.
questions.answer:
◦ State = data R^ remembers between C^ renders.
◦ useState / useReducer manage local state.
◦ Each r() receives a state snapshot.
◦ setState requests an update; current snapshot stays unchanged.
◦ R^ queues updates and calculates next state.
◦ State updates should preserve immutability.
◦ State belongs to C^ identity + tree position.
questions.underTheHood:
◦ R^ associates H^ state w1 C^ Fiber.
◦ setState enqueues an update.
◦ Scheduler assigns update priority.
◦ Multiple updates can be batched.
◦ R^ processes update queue during r().
◦ Object.is() compares previous and next state.
◦ Same state can allow R^ to skip unnecessary work.
◦ Commit applies necessary DOM updates.
pitfalls: ◦ Use functional updater when next state depends on previous state.
◦ Same Object.is() value can skip updates.
◦ Changing key / C^ type can reset state.
followUps: ◦ How does R^ preserve or reset state?
questions.recall:
◦ State → C^ memory.
◦ setState → Queue → Schedule → r() → Commit.
◦ Snapshot ≠ immediate mutation.
◦ Object.is() → equality bailout.
◦ Position + type + key → identity.
